newsitem.title: INDIA: India fishermen end blockade of harbours.
newsitem.headline: India fishermen end blockade of harbours.

text.p: Indian fishermen on Thursday called off a blockade against part-foreign owned trawlers using harbours in nine states along the country's coastline, their leaders said.
The fishermen, who began their protest on Wednesday, are demanding cancellation of licences to part-foreign joint ventures involved in deep sea fishing.

"We called off the agitation following an assurance from the government that the joint venture licences will be cancelled," said Vijay Bhandarkar, president (Bombay region) of the National Fish Workers' Forum.
Bhandarkar said trawlers owned by the joint ventures would not be allowed to operate beyond April 9. Deep sea fishing licences issued for 50 other trawlers also would be cancelled, he said.
Fishermen have argued that mechanised trawlers are depleting India's fishing grounds and represent unfair competition.

Bhandarkar said 7.5 million people were directly involved in fishing, and another 50 million depended on fishing for a living. He said the government had approved the joint ventures for deep sea fishing after it liberalised the economy in 1991 but an official committee had subsequently recommended cancellation of their licences.
